newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia increases motor fuels, oils prices.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia increases motor fuels, oils prices.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it will increase the maximum-allowable retail prices of motor petrol and motor oil by 0.50 crown per litre, effective on August 1.
The hikes meant the maximum retail price, including taxes, on 95 octane lead-free petrol would be 22.60 crowns per litre, 23.00 crowns for 98-octane, and 21.30 per litre for all motor oils.
In a statement, the ministry said the price hike was linked to the recent increase in the consumer tax for the motor fuels.
Earlier this month, Slovakia's government approved an average 10 percent increase in energy prices for corporate consumers, effective August 1, 1997.
Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said the price hike was expected to boost producer prices by an average "two to three percentage points."
The Slovak producer price index (PPI) rose 0.2 percent, month-on-month, in June, putting prices 3.7 percent higher than in the same month of the previous year.
